caption: NCAA v. Governor of New Jersey
citation_line: NCAA v. Governor of New Jersey, 926 F. Supp. 2d 551 (D.N.J. 2013), aff’d sub nom. Nat’l Collegiate Athletic Ass’n v. Christie, 730 F.3d 208 (3d Cir. 2013)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Shipp granted summary judgment and a permanent injunction against New Jersey’s 2012 sports-wagering law, holding that PASPA was a valid exercise of the commerce power and did not commandeer the State.
qualification_rationale: The litigation was nationally consequential: it determined whether states could legalize sports betting and produced a major Supreme Court federalism decision.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit affirmed in a divided precedential opinion, holding that PASPA imposed no affirmative command on the States and so did not offend the anti-commandeering rule. That reasoning was later abrogated by Murphy v. NCAA, 584 U.S. 453 (2018), which arose from the separate 2014 proceeding.
decision_selection_note: ECF 142 of two published Shipp decisions on this docket. The Murphy reversal attaches to the 2014 proceeding at 61 F. Supp. 3d 488, not to this one.
